question_text: Filing 1: File correctly: Cruz, Dela Cruz, De la Cruz, Delos Cruz

options.text: Dela Cruz, De la Cruz, Cruz, Delos Cruz
Cruz, De la Cruz, Dela Cruz, Delos Cruz
De la Cruz, Dela Cruz, Cruz, Delos Cruz
Delos Cruz, Cruz, Dela Cruz, De la Cruz

hint_ladder.title: Orient
hint_ladder.text: This is all about how we treat those fancy Spanish prefixes like 'De la', 'Dela', and 'Delos' when filing alphabetically. The key question is: do we ignore them, or do we treat them as part of the surname?

hint_ladder.title: Rule
hint_ladder.text: In Philippine civil service filing, prefixes are considered part of the surname. So 'De la Cruz' is filed under 'D', not 'C'. And here's the tricky part: when comparing prefixes, spaces matter. A space comes before any letter in the alphabet.

hint_ladder.title: Apply
hint_ladder.text: First, group by first letter. 'Cruz' starts with C, while the others start with D. Now, among the D surnames, compare letter by letter: 'De la' (D, e, space, l, a) vs 'Dela' (D, e, l, a). Since space comes before 'l', 'De la' comes first. Then 'Dela' vs 'Delos': 'a' comes before 'o', so 'Dela' before 'Delos'. Now, where does 'Cruz' fit? Since all have the same root 'Cruz', the one without a prefix is filed after those with prefixes.

hint_ladder.title: Nearly Give Away
hint_ladder.text: So the order is: De la Cruz (space before 'l'), then Dela Cruz (a before o), then Cruz (no prefix, after prefixed ones), then Delos Cruz. That matches option C.

A.text: This order puts Dela Cruz before De la Cruz. A smart student might think 'Dela' looks simpler, but alphabetically, 'De la' has a space after 'e', and in the alphabet, a space comes before the letter 'l'. So 'De la' should actually come first. It's a subtle trap that catches many people.

B.text: This order puts Cruz first, which seems logical because 'C' comes before 'D'. But here's the twist: when surnames share the same root (all are 'Cruz' at heart), the one without a prefix is filed after those with prefixes. So Cruz comes after De la and Dela, not before. It's a common mistake to think 'no prefix' means 'first'.

C.text: Correct! This follows the filing rule perfectly: prefixes are part of the surname, spaces matter (so 'De la' before 'Dela'), and among same-root surnames, the one without a prefix comes after those with prefixes. Well done!

D.text: This order starts with Delos Cruz, but 'Delos' has 'o' as its third letter, while 'De la' has a space and 'Dela' has 'a'. Since 'a' and space both come before 'o', Delos should be last among the D surnames. It's easy to mix up the order when you're rushing.

next_time_rule: When filing surnames with prefixes like 'De la', 'Dela', 'Delos', treat the prefix as part of the surname. Compare letter by letter, including spaces (space comes before any letter). And remember: among same-root surnames, the one without a prefix comes after those with prefixes.

First, look at the first letter of each surname. 'Cruz' starts with C, while the other three start with D.
